page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, providing 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, backed by instruction extensions including AVX-512 and hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. Memory capacity is configured at 384.0 GB of RAM, adhering to an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage consists of a direct-attached 1933 GB local SSD, while accelerated graphics processing is absent with zero GPUs installed.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput capabilities, specifically in large-block uncached read and write bandwidth tests where the instance reached 230.36 GB/sec and 111.32 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of measured systems. General compute evaluations reveal middle-tier performance, marked by a Geekbench multi-core score of 13298.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 39476.15. Data caching and key-value workloads achieve balanced results, logging 38.55 million Redis SET operations per second and 38.47 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Compute-bound text processing and large language model inference show clear constraints; text generation with a 7B model ran at 7.59 tokens per second, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 8.76 GB/sec, settling in the bottom quartile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48ds_v4 delivers high memory density alongside integrated local solid-state storage, eliminating the need for immediately attached external storage for caching or scratch disks. Workloads requiring extreme single-thread performance or tensor processing will face hardware limitations due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. As configured, the instance is well suited for high-capacity relational and in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning systems, data warehousing transformations, and in-memory caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v4 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz, delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores on an x86_64 architecture. The server features 384.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes 1933 GB of local SSD scratch storage without integrated GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, it exhibits top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 230 GB/sec for reads and 111 GB/sec for writes, alongside mid-range multi-core CPU metrics such as a PassMark CPU score of 39476.15 and 38.55 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, sequential single-thread compression and large language model inference demonstrate lower relative throughput. The hardware configuration makes this server suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, relational databases, data analytics, and distributed caching infrastructures.
